title: Factors affecting enzymes
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:35:38Z autoreview: cleared with the fix (b wording)

match.reason: The bank point is about what biotechnology is, not about the factors (temperature, pH, substrate and enzyme concentration) that change enzyme reaction rates, so no bank point teaches the new idea.

draft.title: Factors affecting enzymes
card: Temperature changes the rate of an enzyme reaction. As it rises towards the optimum, particles collide more often and with more energy, so the rate rises.
Above the optimum temperature, the enzyme's shape starts to change. The active site no longer fits the substrate, and the enzyme is denatured. Denaturation is usually permanent.
pH also affects the shape of the active site. Each enzyme has an optimum pH. Away from it, the rate falls, and an extreme pH can denature the enzyme.
More substrate raises the rate until all active sites are busy, then the rate levels off. More enzyme raises the rate if there is enough substrate to use it.
draft.remember: Rate rises towards the optimum, then falls once shape is lost. Concentration raises the rate until something runs out.

a.q: A student heats an enzyme solution well above its optimum temperature, then cools it back to the optimum. Why does the reaction stay slow?
opts: The enzyme was denatured, so the active site no longer fits
The substrate was used up while the solution was hot
The cooling made particles collide less often than before
The enzyme was made smaller, so it binds less substrate
a.why: High temperature changed the enzyme's shape, and denaturation is usually permanent. Cooling does not restore the active site. Fewer collisions at lower temperature would only slow the rate, not keep it low at the optimum.
a.clue: Think about what happens to the active site's shape.

b.q: Mei adds more substrate to an enzyme reaction that is already at its optimum temperature and pH. The rate stops rising. What is the most likely reason?
opts: All the enzyme's active sites are already occupied
The extra substrate has denatured the enzyme
The pH has moved away from the optimum
The enzyme has been used up and cannot work again
b.why: Once every active site is busy, extra substrate cannot be processed any faster, so the rate levels off. Substrate does not denature an enzyme, and the brief says temperature and pH were already at the optimum.
b.clue: Count the active sites, not the substrate.

a.best: The enzyme was denatured, so the active site no longer fits

b.best: All the enzyme's active sites are already occupied

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'the brief says temperature and pH were already at the optimum'. 'The brief' is an unexplained term; it should say 'the question'.
